newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Vienna finance boss says "yes" to finmin job.
newsitem.headline: Vienna finance boss says "yes" to finmin job.

text.p: Vienna City finance chief Rudolf Edlinger confirmed on Friday he would take over as Austrian finance minister and said he would tackle what he termed a difficult job with optimism.
"I will dedicate the necessary energy to this tough task," Edlinger, a Social Democrat, told Austrian radio in a first reaction to his appointment.
Viktor Klima, chancellor-designate and outgoing finance minister, said he considered Edlinger well-equipped to prepare Austria for European Economic and Monetary Union.
"I think Edlinger is an excellent choice," Klima said after a meeting with President Thomas Klestil.

He will name his full Social Democratic ministerial team on Monday. No changes are expected among ministers of the conservative People's Party, which governs in coalition with the dominant Social Democrats.
The treasury post became vacant over the weekend when Franz Vranitzky named Klima his successor as chancellor and Social Democratic Party leader.

Edlinger, 56, has served as the City of Vienna's finance councillor since November 1994 and has borne responsibility for by far Austria's biggest regional budget, with annual expenditure of around 134 billion schillings ($11.68 billion).
"Vienna is losing an outstanding finance chief and Austria is gaining an excellent finance minister," Austrian radio quoted Vienna mayor Michael Haeupl as saying.

Edlinger, a professional lithographer, was a key player in a political team that two weeks ago hammered out a coalition deal over the sale of Austria's most famous bank Creditanstalt to market leader Bank Austria.
The heavy-set smoker had insisted earlier this week that he was not a candidate to take over the finance portfolio and had set his sights on retirement by the year 2000.

Klima's first choice for finance minister Burgenland regional government leader Karl Stix turned down the job on Thursday because of bickering within the regional coalition of Social Democrats and People's Party.
Burgenland People's Party refused to guarantee its backing for a Social Democrat to replace Stix as regional government head if he departed for Vienna.
Klima insisted that he had not been forced into taking an inferior candidate in Edlinger.
"I had a choice of two excellent candidates," he said. ($1=11.47 schillings)
